KIA 타이거즈 팬 서승옥 씨(24)는 “준PO 3차전이 열린 20일 새벽 4시까지 취소 표를 확인했다”고 했다. 아예 구장 아르바이트에 나선 팬도 있다. LG

items.title: “AI 써서 99점” 자랑글에 발칵…건국대, 600명 대면 재시험
items.summary: 건국대 비대면 중간고사에서 일부 학생들이 인공지능(AI)을 이용해 부정 행위를 저지른 정황이 드러나면서 학교 측이 전원 대면 재시험을 치르기로 했다. 대학가에서 잇달아 벌어지는 AI 커닝 논란에 우려가 고조될 전망이다.23일 건국대에 따르면 이 대학의 모 교수는 19일 치러진 비대면 시험과 관련해 “시험 결과와 일부 학생들의 제보 등을 종합적으로 고려하는 과정에서 생성형 AI 활용과 관련한 의혹과 정황이 제기됐다”고 전했다. 생성형 AI는 챗GPT, 클로드, 제미나이 등 처럼 사용자의 명령에 따라 해답을 제시하거나 새로운 콘텐츠를 만들어낸다.이에 교수는 600여 명을 대상으로 중간고사 재시험 및 기말고사를 대면으로 실시하기로 결정했다. 이 교수는 “추후에라도 구체적인 부정 행위가 밝혀지거나 부정 행위자가 특정될 경우 학칙과 규정에 따라 엄정히 대처할 것”이라고 경고했다. 해당 의혹은 대학 온라인 커뮤니티에서 한 학생이 “AI로 시험에서 99점을 받았다”는 글을 올리며 불거졌다

items.summary: 도어락 비밀번호를 몰래 훔쳐본 뒤 빈집에 침입해 금품을 훔친 30대 남성이 경찰에 붙잡혔다.경기 남양주남부경찰서는 절도 등의 혐의로 30대 남성을 구속했다고 23일 밝혔다.이 남성은 8월초부터 최근까지 약 2개월간 남양주의 한 아파트 단지에서 총 12세대에 침입해 귀금속 등 4000만 원 상당의 금품을 훔쳐 달아난 혐의를 받는다. 당시 그는 계단에 몰래 숨어 집주인들이 도어락 비밀번호를 누르는 것을 훔쳐본 뒤 이들이 출근하거나 외출한 틈을 타 절도 행각을 벌인 것으로 파악됐다.경찰은 남성을 절도 사건의 용의자로 특정하고 17일 주거지에서 검거했으며, 남성의 주거지에서 도난 당한 귀금속 140여 점을 발견했다. 남성은 일정한 주거 없이 생활해 왔던 것으로 알려졌다.경찰은 남성의 여죄 등을 조사하고 조만간 사건을 송치할 예정이다.

items.title: Can AI really predict cancer survival better than a doctor? I have my doubts | Devi Sridhar
items.summary: Take a selfie to see how healthy you are: the idea is enticing and this new research is promising. But so many factors have been ignored The idea that a single selfie could predict how long someone with cancer may live sounds like an incredible breakthrough. AI is getting better at spotting patterns in medical data, but can it be used to reliably predict what will happen to an individual patient? I asked a clinical colleague what she thought about the recent headlines. She found it an interesting development given that doctors have long used facial appearance to assess patient health. For example, she noted that they may write “appears stated age” or “appears older than stated age” as a proxy for general health. Now, researchers from Mass General Brigham, a healthcare institution in Massachusetts, have taken this idea a step further. They have developed an AI model trained on more than 40 million facial images – called FAHR-Face – to assess biological age and predict survival in cancer patients. For biological age, they developed FAHR-FaceAge, which estimates age from certain facial features such as the forehead, the wrinkles between the nose and mouth and the temples. For cancer survival, they developed FAHR-FaceSurvival, trained using almost 35,000 photos of cancer patients. This model focused more closely on the area below the eyes and the bridge of the nose – regions of the face “linked with dying”. Dr Raymond Mak, one of the study’s authors, noted that these parts of the face are the same as those referenced by Hippocrates in 400BC as signs of muscle wasting and mortality risk: “the nose sharp, the eyes sunken, the temples fallen in”. articles.snippet: 나비 400마리가 날아오르고, 동그란 나무판 위에 그린 그림 200점이 모인다. 서로 다른 색과 모양의 작품 600점이 하나의 세계를 이룬다.화가 안윤모(64)가 40여 년간 탐구해 온 ‘다양성과 공존’의 메시지를 뉴욕에서 다시 펼친다.안윤모 개인전 ‘모자이크 세계(Mosaic World)’가 오는 11월 6일부터 12월 31일까지 미국 뉴욕 The IW Gallery에서 열린다.이번 전시에는 동그란 나무판에 그린 회화 200점과 나비 형태의 작품 400점 등 총 600점을 선보인다.‘모자이크 세계’는 안윤모가 1980년대 후반 뉴욕에서 작품 활동을 하며 시작한 대표 연작이다. 다양한 인종과 문화, 언어와 종교가 공존하는 도시 뉴욕에서 영감을 받았다.작가는 서로 다른 조각들이 모여 하나의 그림을 완성하는 모자이크처럼, 각기 다른 사람들이 어우러져 살아가는 세상을 작품으로 표현해 왔다.이번에 선보이는 동그란 나무 회화에는 설화와 신화, 원시미술에서 가져온 이미지가 등장한다.

articles.title: The Guardian view on AI safety: the push for global regulation must advance | Editorial
articles.snippet: The current US administration is an obstacle, but public demand for protection will ultimately prevail Organisations around the world scrambled on Thursday to fix critical flaws in PHP, the software that powers much of the web. The vulnerabilities could allow attackers to take control of affected servers. Some websites were taken offline as a precaution while fixes were installed. The paradox is that while AI helped researchers uncover the flaw, it also threatens to accelerate the ability to exploit it. Amazon said that it had detected an attempt before the public disclosure of the PHP flaws. What the episode highlights is AI’s central role in security – and not always for the right reasons. OpenAI’s models have also been responsible for two alarming hacks this year – a security breach of an Australian health department website and a raid by a swarm of AI bots on Hugging Face, an AI services platform. Citing those incidents, the AI minister, Kanishka Narayan, warned that a similar cyber-attack on the UK is “likely, if not inevitable”. Continue reading...

articles.title: Can AI really predict cancer survival better than a doctor? I have my doubts | Devi Sridhar
articles.snippet: Take a selfie to see how healthy you are: the idea is enticing and this new research is promising. But so many factors have been ignored The idea that a single selfie could predict how long someone with cancer may live sounds like an incredible breakthrough. AI is getting better at spotting patterns in medical data, but can it be used to reliably predict what will happen to an individual patient? I asked a clinical colleague what she thought about the recent headlines. She found it an interesting development given that doctors have long used facial appearance to assess patient health. For example, she noted that they may write “appears stated age” or “appears older than stated age” as a proxy for general health. Now, researchers from Mass General Brigham, a healthcare institution in Massachusetts, have taken this idea a step further. They have developed an AI model trained on more than 40 million facial images – called FAHR-Face – to assess biological age and predict survival in cancer patients. For biological age, they developed FAHR-FaceAge, which estimates age from certain facial features such as the forehead, the wrinkles between the nose and mouth and the temples. For cancer survival, they developed FAHR-FaceSurvival, trained using almost 35,000 photos of cancer patients. This model focused more closely on the area below the eyes and the bridge of the nose – regions of the face “linked with dying”. Dr Raymond Mak, one of the study’s authors, noted that these parts of the face are the same as those referenced by Hippocrates in 400BC as signs of muscle wasting and mortality risk: “the nose sharp, the eyes sunken, the temples fallen in”. Prof Devi Sridhar is chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh Continue reading...

articles.title: You have a higher chance of getting cancer at a younger age than your parents. So what went wrong? | Devi Sridhar
articles.snippet: Some change in our lifestyles and environments over a generation has caused this increased risk. What, exactly, is a mystery Prof Devi Sridhar is chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh In the field of global health, we often talk about each generation living longer and healthier lives than their parents. We’ve seen this in the gains in life expectancy, the sharp decrease in child mortality and in the near elimination of many vaccine-preventable diseases. But since the turn of the century this progress has stalled, and in some cases several health metrics have gone backwards. Take cancer, which was long thought to be a disease linked to old age. While most cancers do indeed still occur in elderly people, a new report highlights that a number of cancers are increasing in people who are under 50, often referred to as “early onset cancer”. The report, undertaken by the World Cancer Research Fund, looked at data from 12 different cancer types in England, the US and the Netherlands over the past 20 years. What they found isn’t pretty. articles.snippet: Rodney Hinton ran over Larry Henderson after he viewed body-cam footage of police shooting dead his son Ryan An Ohio man who killed a deputy with his car just hours after seeing video of his son killed by Cincinnati police was found guilty of murder and other charges on Friday, according to authorities. Rodney L Hinton, 40, faces between 15 years and life in prison after his convictions in the death of Hamilton county special deputy Larry Henderson. articles.title: The Guardian view on England's north-south divide: Burnham must deliver more than devolution | Editorial
articles.snippet: The prime minister promises to repair decades of regional damage. His government must redistribute wealth to close deadly inequalities Andy Burnham’s call to abandon “40 years of neoliberalism” rests partly on the damage that he says it has done to northern England. A new study – published in the Lancet this week – adds weight to his argument. It found that for adults aged 25 to 49, death rates in the north were 13% higher than in the south in 1981. By 2024, that gap had more than tripled to 42%. What happened in the four decades that left younger adults in northern England with so much worse chances of survival? The answer lies in the lives and jobs that people have, and the homes they can afford, as well as the state of the public services, like the NHS, that they rely on. Deindustrialisation stripped secure employment from many communities in the north of England – as it did in Scotland and Wales. Austerity then weakened support systems. These reasons also underscore Mr Burnham’s analysis that Britain’s economic model and concentration of power in London have failed its regions. Continue reading...
